title: Private support regime in calendar 2050: declared scheme parameters (FES 2050 plan task Y11, decisions 4, 6, 19, 22)

gas_gbp_per_mwh_thermal.source: FES 2025 CP1 base case 2050 (28.72 EUR/MWh 2025 / 1.17, then / 1.0384 CPIH), task Y1
gas_gbp_per_mwh_thermal.source_page: plan Part 4 Y1 status table; resources/FES/fes2025_future_costs_2050.json when built

biomass_gbp_per_mwh_thermal.source: config/defaults.yaml marginal_costs.future_costs.cases.central.fuel_prices.biomass (the HT50 fallback_case: FES publishes no biomass price)

commodity_prices.note: A caller with the solved year passes the run's own prices; these are the defaults the parameter tables are built with.

efficiency.source: config/defaults.yaml marginal_costs.future_costs.efficiency_defaults (the model's dispatch efficiencies); CCS Gas 0.47 from the 2050 study (DESNZ Electricity Generation Costs 2025 Annex A, 2050; user, 26 Oct 2026)

variable_om_gbp_per_mwh.source: config/defaults.yaml marginal_costs.future_costs.cases.central.variable_om; CCS Gas from the 2050 study (user, 26 Oct 2026): DESNZ EGC 2025 Annex A variable O&M 6 plus the CO2 transport and storage flow charge at 34.5 GBP/t (the reformer's) on 0.183 x 0.90 / 0.47 = 0.3504 tCO2 captured per MWh, 12.09

biomass_emission_factor_tco2_per_mwh_the.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines vol. 2 table 2.2, wood/wood waste default 112 tCO2/TJ (biogenic)

dpa.form: Availability payment (rate x net dependable capacity x availability of low-carbon capacity) plus a variable payment that keeps the plant just ahead of an unabated reference CCGT in merit, with gainshare. NZT Power DPA (LCCC, 19 Nov 2024) and CMA SAU report (Jul 2024); hydrogen power by decision 22 (same form, declared).

term_years.source: NZT Power DPA: expiry at the 15th anniversary of the earlier of the Start Date and the last day of the Target Commissioning Window (research Y5/Y11/Y12 section 3); scheme 10 to 15 years

first_modelled_build_year.source: NZT Power (742.91 MW, FID Dec 2024, commissioning about 2028) ends about 2043, so no CCS plant in 2050 is on it; every 2050 DPA is a modelled later agreement

dpa.availability_payment_basis: cost plus the private rate: APR = (capex x CRF(private rate, economic life) + fixed O&M ex-DESNZ insurance + D4(a) insurance + use of system) / expected availability, from the build year's Y2 vintage row

expected_availability.source: declared: a DPA pays on the availability of low-carbon capacity; 0.90 matches the NESO 2030/31 CCGT de-rating factor (0.9048)

use_of_system_gbp_per_kw_year.source: DESNZ EGC 2025 Annex A row 37, Gas CCUS 900MW and CCHT 900MW (4,400 GBP/MW/yr)

variable_payment_carriers.source: user, 26 Oct 2026 (supersedes decisions 35 and 38 for hydrogen): the government's hydrogen-to-power response (DESNZ, Dec 2024, p.29) proceeds with a DPA-style availability payment but has not adopted a variable payment, which it says 'could create market distortions'; LCP and Frontier for DESNZ (Dec 2023) found a dispatch incentive 'would not reduce costs to society'. Hydrogen power's DPA is an availability payment with gainshare only; gas CCS keeps the NZT variable payment.

variable_payment_margin_gbp_per_mwh.source: declared: 'just ahead' of the reference plant in merit

reference_plant.source: NZT DPA: a daily top-up benchmarked on a reference unabated CCGT (research section 3); used for hydrogen power too (decision 22)

gainshare_share.source: declared: the NZT gainshare terms are redacted; half of the annual energy margin (market revenue less short-run cost) above the threshold is returned

gainshare_threshold_gbp_per_kw_year.source: declared: the availability payment already recovers full cost, so every pound of energy margin is above the threshold

transport_and_storage_fixed.source: ECC full business case (June 2025) section 5.6.1, via the 2030 remaining_ccs line: T&S revenue support to NEP is Exchequer-funded, not a bill charge

dpa.capacity_market: DPA units cannot hold a Capacity Market agreement while the DPA is live (capacity_market.CM_INELIGIBLE_SUPPORT)

beccs.form: Declared dispatchable CfD on the electricity leg (as the 2030 Power BECCS line and its CCS levy treatment); the carbon-removal leg is paid off-bill (lever beccs_removal_funding, default off-bill).

term_years.source: Power BECCS 15 years (DESNZ business model update, Dec 2023; config contract_term_years_by_round.POWER_BECCS)

removal_price_gbp_per_tco2.source: declared: negative emissions valued at the 2050 carbon price (FES CP2, task Y1) through the off-bill removals contract

beccs.note: The 2030 Drax Power BECCS contract (POWER_BECCS, 2030/31 + 15 years) has expired by 2050.

term_years.source: Ofgem LDES window 1 minded-to decision (26 Jun 2026): 25-year terms; 16 projects, 7,645 MW / 136.9 GWh

carriers.source: vintage-table row nearest each FES 2050 duration (LAES 4.1 h, CAES declared 6 h, PHS 17 h)

first_build_year.source: declared: every LDES vintage from window 1 on holds a cap and floor; pre-2026 pumped hydro is merchant

floor_rate.source: config/defaults.yaml public_ownership.consumer_bill.ldes_cap_and_floor.floor_return.real_rate_by_case.private (the 2030 private floor: a debt-like 4.5% real, CEPA 2025 BBB-)

cap_rate_basis.source: declared: Ofgem's cap gives an equity-like return; workbook v2.0 Sc1 Operative cost of equity, pre-tax (snapshot cost_of_equity_pre_tax), of the Novel LDES row (F29, 26 Oct 2026)

above_cap_returned_share.source: declared: as the interconnector regime (Ofgem OFG1164 section 4.6, revenue above the cap returned via TNUoS)

ldes_cap_and_floor.recovery: final demand, like a network charge (the 2030 ldes_cap_and_floor.recovery_denominator)
ldes_cap_and_floor.capacity_market_revenue: counted in the revenue tested against the floor and the cap, as the 2030 public account nets it
